name: Outschool
line: Outschool lists live classes by independent teachers. AMP is one math program that chooses every problem.
description: AMP vs Outschool: live classes taught by independent teachers, against one math program that places, explains and reviews every day.
verdict: Outschool gives a child a live teacher, classmates and more than 100,000 classes to choose from [1]. Its classes are taught by independent teachers, each teacher submits a class for Outschool's approval, and the family enrolls in the classes it picks [2][6]. AMP is one program from counting to precalculus that places the learner, chooses every problem, explains every answer and brings old skills back on a schedule.

reasons.title: One math path instead of a list of classes
reasons.body: Outschool classes are taught by independent teachers, and each teacher submits a class for approval against Outschool's standards for content, learning goals and teacher expertise [2]. Families enroll in individual classes, and Outschool's AI helps them find classes and teachers [6][11]. So the order of math is the set of classes a family picks. AMP holds 336 skills on one map from counting to precalculus, places the learner within the first 24 problems, keeps a level in each of 14 strands and chooses every problem after that.

reasons.title: Practice any day, with every answer explained
reasons.body: An Outschool live class meets by video at scheduled times, and most also involve independent work before or after the meetings [3]. AMP is there whenever the learner sits down, with no fixed session length. After each answer it shows right or wrong, the correct answer and the worked steps. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged a larger effect than feedback that only marks right or wrong [17].

reasons.title: The same teaching for every learner
reasons.body: Outschool screens and background-checks its teachers and asks for "teaching experience, subject matter expertise, or a unique passion" [2]. Common Sense Media notes that teaching credentials are not required and that inconsistent course quality is possible [9]. In AMP every problem type has a one-step hint that never gives the answer, a written lesson with a worked example, and full worked steps. Anyone can read them in the public code.

reasons.title: Old skills come back without anyone planning it
reasons.body: Each Outschool class is its own teacher's, approved against standards for content and learning goals [2], and its independent work comes before or after its meetings [3]. Bringing back skills from earlier classes falls to the teachers and the family. In AMP a skill is Strong after four of the last five answers right without help, two misses in a row send practice back to what it builds on, and learned skills return after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics. In a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks, on the researchers' own test [16].

reasons.title: A record of the level, not only the classes
reasons.body: Outschool does not offer credit for classes, and sharing grades or transcripts must be coordinated directly between parents and teachers [2]. Its AI gives families summaries of what a learner is experiencing in class [11]. AMP shows the level in every strand with its likely range, the skills earned and time by day and skill, in a record that opens to the actual problems. It prints progress reports and report cards.

reasons.title: A flat price and a 30-day refund
reasons.body: A recurring weekly Outschool class is charged as a subscription on Sunday mornings [3]. A membership is refunded in full only within 24 hours of the first month's purchase and only if no credits were used; renewal charges are not refunded [7]. For a personal payment, Outschool's Learning Experience Pledge returns a voucher, not cash [8]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child, and any personal payment is refunded in full within 30 days, no reason needed.

rows.price: Each class has its own listed price, paid per class or with credits from a monthly membership [6]. Check current prices on Outschool's site.
rows.buyers: Families, plus schools and charters by purchase order [13]. Public funds accepted in select states through ClassWallet, Step Up for Students, Odyssey and others [10].
rows.range: More than 100,000 live classes across subjects, ages 1 to 18 [1]. The family enrolls in each math class it picks [6].
rows.start: The family picks a class, helped by Outschool's AI class discovery and teacher matching [6][11].
rows.teaching: A teacher on live video at set times, or pre-recorded lessons with teacher feedback [3][4]. Common Sense Media says inconsistent course quality is possible [9].
rows.next: The family enrolls in the next class. Outschool's AI suggests classes and teachers that may fit [6][11].
rows.mastery: Each teacher decides on any grade or assessment; certificates of completion are at the teacher's discretion [2].
rows.review: Most live classes add independent work before or after meetings [3]. No scheduled review found in its published materials [2][3].
rows.print: No workbooks found in its published materials [2][4]. Self-paced lessons can be saved for offline viewing in its mobile app [4].
rows.adult: Choose and enroll in classes, manage payment, arrange any grade with the teacher, and monitor participation [2][6][9].
rows.reports: AI summaries of what a learner experiences in class [11]. No credit for classes; grades or transcripts coordinated directly with the teacher [2].
rows.evidence: No entry in Evidence for ESSA and no intervention report in the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [14][15].

theirs: Outschool describes itself as an educational platform of online classes for ages 1 to 18, taught by independent teachers. Its help center counts more than 100,000 live online classes and more than 900,000 learners in 174 countries, in subjects from "tap dance to fractions" [1]. Teachers apply to teach, and each new class must be approved against Outschool's standards before it is listed [2].

A live class is a video meeting at scheduled times. One-time classes meet once, short courses run 2 to 7 weeks, semester courses 8 weeks or more, and recurring weekly classes are charged weekly. Most include independent work before or after the meetings [3]. Self-paced classes offer a year of pre-recorded lessons with up to 20 weeks of teacher support [4]. Tutoring is one-on-one, booked from a teacher's available times [5].

Families pay per class or buy a monthly membership whose credits pay for classes [6]. The adult chooses the classes and arranges any grade or transcript directly with the teacher [2]. This page compares Outschool's math classes and tutoring with AMP.
credit: A live teacher who can hear a question and answer it in the moment. AMP has no live teacher or tutor.
One-on-one tutoring, booked from a teacher's available times [5], and classmates. Trustpilot reviewers praise engaging, patient teachers and small groups [12]. AMP has no classmates.
Breadth. More than 100,000 live classes, in subjects far beyond math, for ages 1 to 18 [1]. AMP is math only.
Public funds in many states, through ClassWallet, Step Up for Students, Odyssey and others [10]. AMP takes education funds in three states.
A way to try one class with no membership [6], and a mobile app that saves self-paced lessons for offline viewing [4]. AMP has no store app and no offline mode.

theirs: We found no outcome study of Outschool's math classes on the pages we read. Outschool has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no intervention report in the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [14][15]. Its published numbers count reach: more than 900,000 learners in 174 countries [1]. On Trustpilot it scores 4.1 out of 5 across 3,603 reviews [12]. Those measure enrollment and satisfaction, not learning.

We think a study of Outschool as a whole would be hard to design, because each family takes different classes from different teachers. Tutoring itself has a strong record. Across 263 randomized trials, tutoring averaged 0.40 standard deviations, and 0.16 to 0.22 for large U.S. programs measured on standardized tests [18]. Those trials are of tutoring programs, not of Outschool, and we found no study of Outschool tutoring.
ours: A good teacher explains a wrong answer in the room. AMP explains every answer: right or wrong, the correct answer and the worked steps. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in many ages and subjects, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [17]. AMP also brings old skills back on a schedule, mixed with other topics. In a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later against 38% for practice in blocks, on the researchers' own test [16]. We expect daily practice built this way to help a learner keep what a class teaches. That is our bet, and we have committed to measuring it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child learns best with a live teacher and classmates.
You want a tutor for one topic, an hour at a time.
You want one place for many subjects, not only math.
Your education fund is in a state where Outschool is an approved vendor and AMP is not.
amp: You want daily math that runs itself: placed, chosen, checked and reviewed.
Your child is ahead in one part of math and needs more work in another.
You want every answer explained with worked steps, the same way every time.
You want a set yearly or monthly price and a full refund within 30 days.
Your child takes an Outschool class and needs practice on the days between.

questions.question: Is Outschool a math curriculum?
questions.answer: Outschool describes itself as a platform of online classes taught by independent teachers [1]. Each teacher submits a class for approval against Outschool's standards, and the family enrolls in the classes it picks [2][6]. AMP is one math program with one sequence from counting to precalculus.

questions.question: Is AMP more expensive than Outschool?
questions.answer: It depends on how many classes a family takes. Each Outschool class has its own listed price, paid per class or with membership credits; check current prices on Outschool's site [6]. As checked in November 2026, AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child and $399 or $39 for each additional child, with unlimited workbooks.

questions.question: Can we use AMP alongside an Outschool math class?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level in each of 14 strands, then fills the days between classes with practice at that level and review on a schedule.

questions.question: Can ESA funds pay for Outschool or AMP?
questions.answer: Outschool accepts public funds in select states, through ClassWallet, Step Up for Students, Odyssey and others [10]. Charter school funds cannot buy an Outschool membership [13]. AMP accepts Arizona ESA, Arkansas EFA and New Hampshire EFA funds.

questions.question: Has Outschool been shown to raise math scores?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study. Outschool has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no intervention report in the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [14][15].
